text:
incidents-bot: PAGER — metering pipeline emitted late usage spikes for several customers in us-east-1. symptom: delayed emit + duplicate token counts detected. severity: S2. tagging oncall.

elena: seeing the same in the aggregator logs, timestamp gaps around 2024-12-03T17:09Z to 17:14Z. counts replayed later. looks like an upstream flush race.

samir: how many customers impacted / any external overage flags triggered?

elena: preliminary: ~7 mid-size tenants got overage flags; billing-alerts-bot confirmed 5 active flags.

ops-oncall: @elena can you paste the error snippet? also which deploys around that window?

elena: logs snippet: ```2024-12-03T17:09:41Z ERROR emitter: flush failed: write timeout; retry=1
2024-12-03T17:10:04Z WARN aggregator: duplicate token id detected: tx=0x9f...
2024-12-03T17:12:17Z INFO emitter: delayed flush completed (lag=125s)```

maria: Rolling back the aggregator change from today would be fastest if that's the culprit. Can we do a canary rollback?

kevin: I see a deploy at 17:05 that changed batching logic (PR #4123). Metrics show spike in kv-write latency immediately after.

ops-oncall: roll back canary to previous tag on the aggregator in us-east-1. I'll kick it now and monitor.

ops-oncall: /deploy rollback aggregator us-east-1 tag=v1.8.4 -> started

incidents-bot: Deploy rollback started by ops-oncall. ETA ~3m.

samir: billing-alerts-bot — are those overage flags actionable now or auto-resolved? we need a customer-facing note if invoices may be affected.

billing-alerts-bot: 5 flags active: cust-a, cust-b, cust-f, cust-g, cust-z. All flags originated between 17:11 and 17:16 UTC. No auto-resolve triggered.

elena: after rollback, I'm seeing emit latency drop back to baseline. aggregator duplicate warnings stopped. counts in staging reconcile look correct so far.

ops-oncall: rollback succeeded. verifying replay queues are not double-applying events.

kevin: running quick reconcile: `./tools/reconcile --window 2024-12-03T17:00:00Z --2024-12-03T17:30:00Z --dry-run` shows 0 net-overcounts after de-dupe heuristics.

maria: Good. Next steps: 1) manual de-flag for the 5 customers after confirmation, 2) customer comms draft, 3) postmortem and telemetry alert to catch this specific race.

samir: I'll prepare the customer note. Quick question: do we expose any billing lines already? Are invoices affected?

billing-alerts-bot: No invoices generated yet for the window. Charge flags are internal pre-invoice markers.

elena: we'll keep monitoring for 30m and then ask finance to de-flag. Putting a temporary rule to ignore emit events older than 90s to avoid late replay counts until we harden dedupe logic.

ops-oncall: added temporary rule in routing: `ignore.emit.age_threshold=90s` in us-east-1. Watchers: elena, kevin.

kevin: ack. also storing the conflicting batch ids for postmortem: `conflict_ids=["0x9f...","0xab..."]`.

samir: handing off to morning oncall at 02:00 PST — please escalate if duplicates reappear. I'll keep draft of customer comms in #support-drafts and share link here.

incidents-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (rollback + routing rule) at 1748460200. Monitoring continues.

maria: filing incident ticket and tagging for postmortem. assign to elena + kevin for root cause and remediation (dedupe algorithm + stronger emit retries).

elena: noted. will include a regression test for delayed-flush scenarios and add metric `emitter.flush_lag_p95` alert.

samir: thanks team. small follow-up: finance — if de-flagging is manual, please wait for confirmation from elena before reversing flags.

billing-alerts-bot: Acknowledged. awaiting de-flag confirmation.

kevin: last note — no customer data exposure. this was an internal counting anomaly.

maria: closing initial pager. will reopen if anything spikes again. :white_check_mark:
